issues.legal_issue: A claim suit against the government following an attachment-objection proceeding is subject to the statutory requirement of prior notice.
material_facts: In execution of a restitution order, the government sought attachment and sale of property that the claimant said he had purchased from the judgment debtor.
The claimant's objection to the attachment was dismissed, after which he filed a suit to establish his title to the property and prevent its attachment and sale.
The claimant gave written notice to the government before filing the suit; the suit was timely if the notice period counted, but otherwise was barred by limitation.
The lower courts held that the statutory notice requirement did not apply and dismissed the suit as time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The notice requirement applies to a suit brought under Order 21, Rule 63 against the government. The appeal was allowed, the lower courts' decree was set aside, and the suit was remanded for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure uses express, explicit, and mandatory language applying to suits against the government, without an exception for suits under Order 21, Rule 63. Such a proceeding is instituted as a suit by plaint, is broader than the summary investigation under Order 21, Rule 58, and is not merely a continuation of that proceeding or an appeal from its order; the order is the cause of action for the suit. The purpose of notice cannot override the statutory text. Bhagchand Dagadusa v. Secretary of State for India in Council was applied for the principle that section 80 admits of no implied exceptions; Phul Kumari v. Ghanshyam Mishra was explained as addressing court fees, not establishing that such a suit is a continuation or appeal for all purposes; and Amar Nath Dogra v. Union of India was explained as holding that an earlier notice could suffice in the circumstances there, not that notice was unnecessary.

predicates.suit_follows_attachment_objection_order: A party brings a separate claim suit after an order rejecting that party's objection to attachment of property in execution proceedings.
predicates.government_is_defendant: The government is named as a defendant in the claim suit.

issues.definition: When a separate claim suit follows an attachment-objection order and the government is the defendant, prior government notice is required.
